summary.intent: Build an alert agent for a hackathon team (START Hack Munich, Lio challenge 'Keep the Line Running'): analyse Soony's confidential procurement data, detect launch risks, and build a product that polls, extracts, alerts by push/phone and acts by email, with a voice assistant to approve decisions.
summary.outcome: Found the key risks (art books, statues, game cards, sleeves), then built a poller/store, dashboard, supplier mail, Twilio and GPT-Realtime call escalation, and a PWA with push, login, voice assistant tools and reply tracking. Most work is committed locally on unpushed branches, with real verifier cards now in the inbox; phone testing and branch merging remain.

repo: Portal API has only /files, /files/{path}, /archive.zip; there are no webhooks, so change detection must poll and compare SHA-256, and files are replaced under the same name.
Challenge data is confidential: keep it in gitignored data/, never commit it, never put real values in tests or docs; use example.com placeholders.
Team rules in CLAUDE.md: no em dashes, commit on your own with one commit per topic and no attribution trailers, confirm before every push, never open PRs unasked.

Akshat's dashboard card contract uses data/store/*cards*.json, decisions.json, mode.json and actions.json with a reply field; the inbox showed only sample fixtures (supplier-one.example.com) until the verifier wrote real cards.
The verifier on origin/integration/verifier generates real cards with supplier to_email from portal profiles; it can be run read-only from a temporary worktree.

The ask-soony-serve tmux session runs code loaded from jonas/alerts, while the working tree is jonas/voice-dashboard, which lacks alerts/openai_calls; restarting serve from this checkout would break call webhooks until branches are merged.
BasicAuth middleware must read the process env only, not .env, or Akshat's tests fail.

code.finding: Replaced browser basic-auth popups with a /login form and 30-day cookie because iPhone home-screen PWAs cannot show the popup, which caused a white screen on reopen; the form body is parsed manually to avoid a dependency.

Realtime session uses server_vad threshold 0.8, interrupt_response false, near_field noise reduction, English-only transcription and instructions to ignore background speech; this fixed Chinese-character transcripts from chatter.
Transcript ordering fixed by inserting a placeholder line when the user stops speaking; hold-to-talk was tried and removed because the user wanted a phone-call feel.
Service worker handles push and notificationclick, opening /?card=ID&talk=1, which shows the Answer screen.
Voice tools get_card_details, send_supplier_email and escalate_to; send requires explicit confirmed:true, only sends pre-written drafts, and only to the six portal supplier addresses.

workflow: Use a subagent for bulk cross-checks (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans) and render scanned PDFs to images to read them.
Re-check the portal against the earlier snapshot while working; 5 new files arrived within 37 minutes of the first download.
Check for teammates' pushes and team workflow files (CLAUDE.md, PROGRESS.md) before writing code; do not edit a teammate's PROGRESS.md.
Confirm every paid action first, including automatic fallbacks; the user objected when a script bought a US Twilio number unasked.
Docs and artifact edits: read the doc first to check for outside edits before replacing a section.

friction: Portal token was empty at start, causing 401 and blocking data access until the user supplied it.
Twilio trial limits (verified numbers only, Url mode instead of inline TwiML, no German number without a business regulatory bundle) caused repeated detours and a script bought a US number unasked.
Cloudflare tunnel quirks: route dns bound to the wrong tunnel, second-level subdomain cert error, QUIC blocked so http2 was needed.
Realtime voice picked up background noise and chatter, needing several rounds of VAD and instruction tuning.
iPhone PWA showed a white screen after reopen because of basic-auth 401.
A real alert email was accidentally sent to a real address, so alert emails became opt-in.
GitHub was unreachable overnight, so branches remained unpushed.
The sample cards had placeholder supplier addresses that could not send mail until real verifier cards were installed.
open_items: Push jonas/alerts, jonas/voice-dashboard and the spec commit 84b4134 once the user approves, and tell Akshat; merge everything onto one team branch before the demo.
Verify the reply-tracking work (replies.py poller attaching the Hwaseong reply to the card, plus the hang-up fix) and finish its commit; the transcript ends before the result was reported.
Wire critical cards to automatic push, then a Twilio plus GPT-Realtime call if unanswered.
Test the PWA, push, English transcription and transcript ordering on a real iPhone.
Optional revise_draft tool so the draft can be changed during a conversation, with re-confirmation before sending.
Hand-in by Sun 22 Nov 12:00: demo script, deck, video of 3 minutes or less, README paragraph and deployed prototype.
Decide on a German phone number later; it needs a business bundle.
